questions.question: Why use a Session and a timeout in requests, and how do you set them?
questions.title: Sessions and Timeouts in requests
questions.direct_answer: A requests.Session reuses the underlying TCP connection (and cookies/headers) across multiple calls, making a sequence of calls to the same host faster and easier to configure (set auth/headers once). A timeout is the max time to wait for a connection/response; without one, a hung server blocks your call (and your program) indefinitely. Set a timeout on every call (timeout=N seconds, or separate connect/read tuples) and prefer a Session for repeated calls. Both are basic production hygiene: sessions for speed and convenience, timeouts for safety.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you can explain why a Session is faster (connection reuse) and why a timeout is mandatory (a hung server blocks forever without one).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Not setting a timeout (a hung server blocks forever) or using requests.get in a loop instead of a Session (slow, no reuse).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: A Session reuses the TCP connection (faster, cookies/headers once); a timeout caps the wait (mandatory — no timeout = block forever). Both are production hygiene.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: A requests dot Session reuses the underlying TCP connection across multiple calls to the same host, which avoids the TCP and TLS handshake overhead on every call and makes a sequence of calls faster. It also holds cookies and lets you set auth and headers once for all calls. A timeout is the maximum time to wait for a connection and response, and without one a hung or slow server blocks your call — and your program — indefinitely. Set timeout equals N seconds, or a connect-and-read tuple, on every call, and use a Session for repeated calls to the same host. Both are basic production hygiene: sessions for speed and convenience, timeouts for safety against hung servers. The common mistakes are not setting a timeout, which lets a hung server block forever, using requests.get in a loop instead of a Session, which is slow because it does a new TCP handshake each time, and setting the timeout on the Session but not the call or vice versa.

sections.title: A Session and timeouts
sections.content:
```python
import requests

# (1) SESSION: reuse the connection; set headers/auth ONCE.
s = requests.Session()
s.headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer <token>'
s.headers['Accept'] = 'application/json'
for user_id in range(10):
    r = s.get(f'https://api.example.com/users/{user_id}', timeout=10)
    #   Reuses the TCP connection -> faster; auth header set once.

# (2) TIMEOUT: a single value, or a (connect, read) tuple.
r = requests.get(url, timeout=10)                 # 10s total
r = requests.get(url, timeout=(3.05, 30))         # 3.05s connect, 30s read
#   Without timeout, a hung server blocks the call INDEFINITELY.
```
